page: Vultr voc-m-24c-192gb-4800s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server configured with 24 vCPUs and 192.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The system is powered by an AMD EPYC processor operating at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, featuring 12 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU allocation is shared. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and FMA instructions. Local storage is provided via a bundled 4800 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark testing, this server demonstrates strong memory performance, particularly in large-block read and write operations. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 488.87 GB/sec, and write bandwidth reached 225.61 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. CPU performance is also robust, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core metrics scoring in the top 25%. Passmark CPU tests yielded a score of 51801.15, also in the top 25%. However, decompression and database operations, such as Redis SET operations at 55.54 million operations per second, align with average middle-tier performance.

The primary tradeoff of this configuration is its shared CPU allocation, which may introduce performance variability under sustained, high-intensity compute workloads compared to dedicated-core instances. Despite this, the server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads due to its dense 192.0 GB RAM capacity and substantial 4800 GB NVMe SSD storage. This resource profile is highly suitable for large-scale databases, memory-cached applications, data indexing, and moderate-scale web serving.
